title: Geneva Rising Revisited
premise: Yara Almeida, a Geneva-based interpreter haunted by a translation failure that helped trigger the 'incident' two years ago, is assigned to a doomed border peace delegation. When a burner phone rings with the voice of their supposedly dead mentor, Elias, Yara learns a false-flag attack is scheduled to coincide with a checkpoint shift change—and that Elias may have orchestrated the original incident. Torn between loyalty to the man who made them an interpreter and the truth that could save hundreds, Yara races through Geneva's diplomatic underworld to decode the plot, discovering their own family's hidden inheritance is the payment funding it. In the climax, Yara publicly mistranslates a live negotiation to expose the conspirators, forcing the attack's abort at the cost of Elias's life, and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Noor Eriksen is a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind the glass of international summits before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about the invisible people who stand between languages—and between peace and catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Glass Booth
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. We open mid-interpretation at a fractious pre-summit briefing, Yara flawless on the surface while insomnia frays them underneath. A colleague notes they flinched at the word 'checkpoint.' The beat is controlled dread: competence as armor.

chapters.title: Assignment to Nowhere
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara is attached to the Alpine Corridor peace delegation—talks everyone privately expects to collapse. They recognize the lead negotiator from the incident. Flashbacks surface the mistranslated phrase Yara can never forget. Beat: reluctant return to the scene of the wound.

chapters.title: A Number That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A courier slips Yara a burner phone in a hotel lobby; no sender, no explanation. That night it rings. Elias's voice—dead for two years—says only: 'You're already inside it.' Beat: vertigo, the past reaching through the glass.

chapters.title: Shift Change at the Border
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with an interlude from delegation security chief Marta Voss. Yara maps the delegation's schedule against the checkpoint rotation and finds a forty-minute gap where an 'accident' could be staged. Marta watches Yara too closely. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Elias, Speaking
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The phone calls continue; Elias claims he faked his death and that the incident was engineered—by him. He offers Yara a choice: help stop the new attack and learn the whole truth. Beat: loyalty and betrayal braided into a single voice.

chapters.title: Found People
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A quiet chapter: dinner with Yara's chosen family—fellow interpreters Amara and Dev, who covered for them after the incident. Yara almost tells them everything, doesn't, and hates themselves for it. Beat: tenderness sharpened by secrecy.

chapters.title: The Almeida Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Following Elias's clue, Yara opens a sealed family file and finds their late father's accounts quietly funding a 'logistics foundation'—the same entity named in the attack's financing. Beat: inheritance revealed as a debt, not a gift.

chapters.title: What Marta Knows
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta reports Yara's odd behavior to a superior who orders her to leave it alone—suspicious in itself. She tails Yara to the archive and pockets a copied ledger page. Beat: the watcher becomes a wildcard.

chapters.title: The First Attempt
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A 'routine' vehicle inspection at the delegation's convoy nearly becomes the accident early. Yara's quick mistranslation buys thirty seconds that save lives—and marks them. Beat: first blood; no more bystander.

chapters.title: Amara Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara notices the burner, the bruise from the convoy, the lies. She confronts Yara gently; Yara deflects, and Amara chooses—without being asked—to stand guard anyway. Beat: found family tested by silence, holding.

chapters.title: Dead Drop at Les Bains
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Elias arranges a meeting at a shuttered bathhouse. Yara sees him alive, scarred, unrepentant about the incident; he reveals the attack's architect sits inside the delegation itself. Beat: the mentor made monstrous, the truth half-delivered.

chapters.title: The Mole's Signature
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Cross-referencing the foundation's payments with delegation access logs, Yara narrows the suspects to three—including, painfully, Dev. Beat: paranoia poisons the safest place Yara has.

chapters.title: Marta's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta confronts Yara with the ledger page and offers a trade: her silence for the truth. Yara tells her everything; Marta admits her superior ordered her to stand down. Beat: two guarded people forming an uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The foundation's charter names a successor trustee: Yara. Their father's fortune isn't funding the attack—it's being stolen to fund it, and Yara's signature can freeze it. Beat: inheritance becomes leverage, and responsibility.

chapters.title: Dev
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev is innocent but compromised: he was coerced into passing one document to save his brother's visa. He confesses to Yara, giving them the document—and a name. Beat: loyalty's cost, truth's relief.

chapters.title: The Architect
chapters.summary: Yara and Marta's alternating POV. The name leads to Deputy Delegate Renard—the man who ordered Marta to stand down and who authored the incident Elias enabled. Renard, sensing exposure, moves the attack up. Beat: the trap tightens from both ends.

chapters.title: Burned
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The burner goes silent; Elias's safehouse is torched. Renard's people hunt Yara through Geneva's night. Amara and Dev hide them, finally fully inside the secret. Beat: found family becomes the only safe house.

chapters.title: Elias's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A dying Elias reaches them one final time: the attack will be triggered by a coded phrase only an interpreter would catch, spoken during the closing session. He asks forgiveness; Yara gives neither yes nor no. Beat: the mentor's end, the student's resolve.

chapters.title: Closing Session
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The doomed summit's final day. Renard delivers his coded line; Yara hears it, must mistranslate it live without tipping him, while Marta locks down the checkpoint gap. Beat: the glass booth becomes a battlefield.

chapters.title: The Word for Stop
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, high-tension climax. Yara's false translation exposes Renard mid-sentence; Marta's team intercepts the strike team at the shift change; Renard is arrested as the 'accident' fails to happen. Beat: the mistranslation that saves, answering the one that didn't.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the inquiry, Yara testifies to the original incident—their failure, Elias's design, their father's stolen money—and surrenders the inheritance claim. Amara and Dev wait outside. Beat: truth as the only inheritance worth keeping.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue. Weeks later, Yara interprets at a small, unglamorous border reopening—talks that actually hold. That night, no burner rings, no phone at all. Yara sleeps through till morning. Beat: quiet, earned peace; invisibility chosen at last.
